title: A quarter of your needs every other day: 12 weeks in adults without obesity [fast_day_quarter, twelve_weeks]
teaser: Adults who were normal weight or overweight ate a quarter of their energy needs every other day, and ate freely in between. [inclusion_bmi, fast_day_quarter, feed_day_free] After 12 weeks, they weighed 5.2 kg less than a control group. [weight_md] On free days, they ate 1856 kcal. [feed_w12] The control group ate 1790 kcal a day. [ctrl_w12]
hook: Every other day, 15 adults ate a single meal of 400 to 600 kcal. [per_group_15, meal_kcal] After 12 weeks, they weighed 5.2 kg less than a control group. [weight_md]
populationPanel: Who this was tested in: 30 adults in Chicago aged 35 to 65, with a BMI of 20 to 29.9. [completed_30, recruited, inclusion_age, inclusion_bmi] That is normal weight or overweight, not obese. [inclusion_bmi] Most were women. [sex_table] None had diabetes or heart disease, or smoked, and all were lightly active. [inclusion_health, inclusion_active] A random draw split them between fasting and eating as usual. [stratified] Fifteen in each group finished. [per_group_15]

card.question: Does fasting every other day help adults without obesity lose weight? [weight_md]
card.headline: After 12 weeks, the fasting group weighed 5.2 kg less than the control group. [weight_md]
card.support: Most of that was fat: 3.6 kg, while lean mass showed no clear difference. [fat_md, lean_ns]

paragraphs: Think of two days as one budget. [-] On a fast day, the fasting group ate one provided meal of 400 to 600 kcal, about a quarter of their needs. [meal_kcal, fast_day_quarter] On the next day, they ate whatever they liked. [feed_day_free]

The plan only works if the free day does not refill the gap. [-] By the end, a free day held 1856 kcal and a fast day 489. [feed_w12, fast_w12] The control group ate 1790 kcal a day. [ctrl_w12] So every two days, the fasting group's budget came out well below the control group's. [feed_w12, fast_w12, ctrl_w12]
The authors saw little or no burst of overeating after a fast, which they call hyperphagia. [no_overeating] Food eaten stayed level on both kinds of day across the 12 weeks. [intake_constant]
The scale followed. [-] After 12 weeks, the fasting group weighed 5.2 kg less than the control group. [weight_md] Of that, 3.6 kg was fat; lean mass showed no clear difference. [fat_md, lean_ns]
Fasting got easier to live with, too. [-] Fullness and satisfaction on fast days rose over the trial, and hunger stayed level. [fullness_up, hunger_ns]

figure.caption: Each bar is the group's average food for that kind of day at the end of the trial, from food records. [feed_w12, fast_w12, ctrl_w12]
figure.alt: Two rows of bars on one scale. [-] Fasting group: fast-day bars at 489 kcal alternate with feed-day bars at 1856 kcal. [fast_w12, feed_w12] Control group: every bar at 1790 kcal. [ctrl_w12]

params.title: Food eaten per day, end of trial

paragraphs: The tested plan ran for 12 weeks. [twelve_weeks] On a fast day: one meal of 400 to 600 kcal, eaten between 12.00 pm and 2.00 pm. [meal_kcal, meal_window] That was 25% of each person's energy needs. [fast_day_quarter] On the next day, people ate freely. [feed_day_free]

On fast days, the trial allowed energy-free drinks, tea, coffee and sugar-free gum, and encouraged plenty of water. [fast_drinks] The provided meals were 30% fat, 15% protein and 55% carbohydrate. [meal_menu]

audit.effect: Body weight at week 12: 5.2 kg lower in the fasting group than in the control group (p < 0.001). [weight_md, weight_down] That is 6.5% of body weight. [weight_pct]
audit.weakEnd: The paper reports no confidence interval. [weight_md] Its ± figures are standard errors, which the read does not turn into a range. [sem] So how far the true difference strays from 5.2 kg stays unknown. [weight_md]
limitations: Small: 15 people a group, for 12 weeks. [limit_small, limit_twelve]
Planned as normal weight against overweight; the authors merged the groups after the fact. [limit_post_hoc]
Food records: people with overweight under-report by about 30%, so the finding of little catch-up eating may be off. [limit_food_records]
audit.missed: The blood-marker claims mix two tests. [-] Triglycerides and LDL particle size differed from controls at week 12, but their changes did not (p = 0.22 and 0.13). [tg_down, ldl_size_up, tg_change_p, ldl_size_change_p] Adiponectin and leptin are the reverse (end-of-trial p = 0.15 and 0.55). [adiponectin_up, leptin_down, adiponectin_w12_p, leptin_w12_p] The authors sized the trial for LDL cholesterol, which showed no clear difference from controls. [power_ldl, ldl_ns]
more: Fat mass: 3.6 kg lower than controls (p < 0.001); lean mass showed no clear difference. [fat_md, fat_down, lean_ns]
CRP was lower than controls on both tests (p = 0.01). [crp_down, crp_change_p]
Total cholesterol and blood pressure showed no clear difference from controls. [chol_ns, bp_ns] HDL, homocysteine and resistin stayed level. [hdl_ns, others_ns]
Kept to the fast-day plan: 98%, by self-report. [adherence]
Thirty-two started and 30 finished; one left because they could not keep to the diet. [randomized_32, completed_30, one_dropout_diet]
Side effects: two mild headaches and one case of constipation, early on. [side_effects]
Funded by a departmental grant; no conflicts of interest. [funding, no_competing]

glossary.plain: Eating much more than usual, here on the day after a fast.
Kilocalories, the unit of food energy that labels usually just call calories.

takeaways: Fasting every other day, adults without obesity weighed 5.2 kg less than a control group after 12 weeks. [weight_md]
Most of the difference was fat; lean mass showed no clear difference. [fat_md, lean_ns]
Small and short, and the authors merged the groups after the fact. [limit_small, limit_twelve, limit_post_hoc]
